argument: Every function has a statically checked return on all terminating source paths and definitely assigned reads. A statically detected cycle or external function is rejected.

Each function has distinct parameter/local registers, return-value registers and one selector. At a call site parameter expressions have been evaluated, the parameters are copied, and the selector is assigned that sites unique natural index before jumping to its fixed entry.

Acyclicity prevents any nested call from activating the current function again. Therefore its local values and selector are not changed by nested functions except for independently validated shared-register allocation. Distinct functions use distinct unallocated register namespaces.

Every return writes all returned values then jumps to that functions static dispatcher. Exactly one equality branch matches its saved site index and returns to that call sites continuation. The continuation copies each return value into a fresh temporary before any later call can replace the helpers return registers.

All impossible selector values enter a self-loop; they cannot fabricate a successful return or HALT. Valid source executions never enter this loop. The entry stub ends at its own HALT only after receiving the actual top-level result.

The inherited liveness analysis uses every possible dispatcher successor, hence a conservative CFG. Its interference graph separates simultaneously needed values, multiple DIVMOD destinations, all inputs and every entry-live zero register from every input. Register coloring can increase interference conservatively but does not merge simultaneously observable values.

By induction on the finite acyclic call graph and each source statement step, raw calls simulate source computations. By the register-liveness invariant the allocated program simulates raw calls. Divergence remains divergence; no separate CALL opcode, oracle or host callback is assumed.
claim: For this acyclic pure source language, shared-call lowering preserves the source execution using only the existing natural-register instruction semantics.

finite_validation.role: Corroboration only; review arguments are not inferred from passing examples.

limitations: This is an independent mathematical/code review, not a proof-assistant replay.
The claim is bound to these exact sources and does not certify future source languages or compiler changes.
The compiled PA checker and HBL conditions require their own separate independent review.
